title: Pulse Run
user: Desktop or keyboard players who want a quick rhythm run in a browser without licensed-song dependence, account setup, or downloadable client.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Row to Glory is a browser Viking rhythm game rendered in one HTML file, showing a lightweight web rhythm game can be compelling.
Playbach.io is introduced directly as a desktop browser rhythm game, an independent current signal for the format.
Fetched Row to Glory page corroborates that a browser rhythm game can package an original themed experience.

recurrence: Two independent browser rhythm releases in spring/summer 2026 indicate renewed interest, while the category is often blocked by music licensing or huge song libraries.
current_workaround: Install a dedicated rhythm game, play an ad-heavy clone, or rely on YouTube/extension-driven copyrighted tracks.
incumbents_and_gap: Osu!-style ecosystems have depth and setup cost; YouTube rhythm add-ons depend on third-party media. Small browser demos rarely make each run structurally different.
smallest_useful_product: A 3-minute keyboard rhythm roguelite with an original generative percussion soundtrack. Between 30-second tracks, choose one modifier that changes note patterns, input lanes, or scoring. Three missed phrases ends a run. Non-goals: imported songs, user charts, copyrighted audio, or competitive ranking.
success_measure: At least 30% of new players finish a first run and 20% start a second build in the same visit.
monetization: one-time — a small original soundtrack and no ads support a finite premium arcade experience.
constraints: Commission or synthesize only original audio; meet keyboard accessibility and honor reduced-motion preference; audio must unlock only after a user gesture.
why_distinct: Run-building gives original, licensable music replay value rather than copying a song-library rhythm game.
